Camera to iPhone

How to transfer digital camera photos to iPhone

For the most reliable full-resolution transfer, connect the camera, storage device, or SD card reader and import with Apple Photos. You can also use the camera maker's app when it preserves the original photo and its metadata.

Quick answer

Choose the connection you have.

SD card reader ↓ Camera or drive ↓ Camera app ↓ Already in Photos ↓

Last updated September 17, 2026

Apple Photos import

Three ways to move the original photos.

01

Use an SD card reader

Insert the card, open Photos, and choose Import. This is usually the simplest path for full-resolution originals.

Best default
02

Connect the camera or drive

Use a compatible cable or adapter. Some devices need additional power before Import appears.

Good for USB-C workflows
03

Use the camera maker's app

Verify that wireless transfer sends the original file, not a resized copy with reduced metadata.

Check one sample first
  1. Connect the deviceUse a compatible adapter, cable, or SD card reader for your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Open Photos and choose ImportThe Import view appears when iOS recognizes the camera or storage device.
  3. Select and importWait for the transfer to finish before disconnecting the device.
  4. Verify a few originalsCheck that the expected photos and capture dates reached the library.
Need device-specific details?

Apple maintains the current connection and import steps in its iPhone User Guide.

Why the Photos map may still be empty

Your photos made it to the iPhone. Their locations may not have.

Import preserves GPS already embedded in a file, but it cannot create coordinates the camera never recorded. If Info shows no map, the photo may still retain the capture time and camera model needed for matching against a GPX track or nearby iPhone photos.

Diagnose before adding anything

Check whether the photo already has a location.

  1. Open a camera photo in PhotosUse an original from the imported batch, not a screenshot or a social-media copy.
  2. Swipe up or tap InfoIf a map and place name appear, Apple Photos already has a library location for that item.
  3. Compare several photosOne image may contain GPS while another does not, especially if location recording was intermittent or files came through different workflows.

If you know the place, use the built-in adjustment steps →

Import questions

Camera photos on iPhone

Why did the capture date transfer but not the location?

Capture time and GPS are separate metadata fields. Most cameras record time; many do not have a GPS receiver or did not have location recording active.

Can I use camera Wi-Fi instead of a card reader?

You can use any workflow that places the original-quality photo in Apple Photos with its camera and capture-time metadata intact. Check a sample file before importing a large batch.

What if the imported photo is only in iCloud?

LensPin may need to download the asset to inspect original metadata or create an optional EXIF edit. See iCloud Photos support.
